When you use the assistant, your message, the files and photos you attach and the project context you choose are sent directly from your device to the provider you selected, such as GitHub Copilot, Pollinations AI, KeylessAI, OpenZoo, Kilo Gateway, maximumsats.com or LLM7.io. What happens to that data there is governed by that provider\'s own privacy policy. Do not send secrets or personal data you would not want that provider to receive.
When the app uses the internet

Passwords for signing keys and the API keys or tokens you give to AI providers are sealed with a key held by the Android Keystore, in secure hardware where the device has it. They are used only to sign your packages or to reach the service you chose, and they are never sent to the developer.

Your projects, source files, unsaved drafts, build outputs, signing keystores, preferences, assistant conversations and the app\'s own log are kept in the app\'s private storage on this device. Android keeps that storage out of reach of other apps. None of it is uploaded to the developer.
What is stored on your device

Apk Builder is an Android development environment that works on your device. This policy explains what the app keeps, what leaves your device and when, and the choices you have. The app has no accounts, no analytics, no advertising and no tracking of any kind.

The AI providers, GitHub, Git hosts and Maven repositories are run by third parties under their own terms. Their availability, limits and answers are outside the developer\'s control. Code an assistant suggests may be wrong; review and test it before you release it.

Signing keys stay on your device. If you lose a key or its password, no one, including the developer, can recover it, and an app published with that key cannot be updated with another. Keep your own backups.

Do not use the app to build or spread malware, to infringe anyone\'s rights or to break the law. You are responsible for what you build and where you publish it, including the licences of the libraries you use and the rules of the stores you upload to.
Your projects, source code, assets and the packages you build belong to you. The app claims no rights over them and does not use them for any purpose of its own.

Apk Builder compiles, packages and signs Android applications on your device. The compiler, resource compiler, dexer, shrinker and signer run on your phone\'s own processor; no step of a build is sent to a server.
By installing or using Apk Builder you agree to these terms. If you do not agree, uninstall the app; nothing is kept once it has been removed.

What this app is, and where to begin

Apk Builder compiles Android packages on this device. There is no server and no desktop toolchain: the compiler, the packager and the signer all run here. Make a project from Home, write your code under Java, then build it.

A project needs a name, a package name such as com.example.app, a version, and the Android versions it runs on. The package name is what Android knows an installed app by, so choose it before you publish rather than after. An icon can be added at any time from Files.
The editor, and what it checks as you type

Files opens a project. Tapping a source file opens the editor, which colours the code and checks it a moment after you stop typing. Names it already knows are offered as you type, and it will jump to where a name was written or list everywhere it is used.
From sources to an APK and a bundle

Build compiles the sources, packs the resources, writes the dex, seals the package and then verifies what it wrote. It produces an APK to install here and a bundle to upload. Every build needs a signing key, and a shared one is made for you the first time.
Keys, passwords, and what a signature proves

Every package is signed. A signature proves the package came from the key that signed it, and Android refuses an update signed by a different key. Keep your key and its password somewhere safe: a lost key cannot be replaced, and the app it signed can never be updated again.
Reading a refusal, and fixing what it names

A refusal names a code, the file and the line it is about, and says what it wants instead. Project health lists what is wrong with a project before a build starts. Where the repair is one this app can make itself, it offers it and shows what it would change first.

This app\'s own log is always readable. To see the whole device, the reading permission is granted once from a computer over ADB.
Reads the log live on this device: this app\'s own process, or the whole device once the reading permission is granted.

Without the reading permission, Android shows an app only its own log. The permission that widens it to the whole device is not one a tap can grant: it is handed over from a computer with ADB, which is why this screen shows you the line to run instead of a switch that would do nothing.

The app holds the internet permission and uses it only when you ask for something that needs it: sending a message to the AI assistant, signing in to GitHub Copilot, cloning a Git repository, or downloading a library your project names from Maven Central or Google\'s Maven repository. The app has no server of its own and sends nothing in the background.

How does the file system work?

This app was made for Android itself. Gradle and the desktop tools were not written for a phone and are not fully supported there. So this carries its own build engine and no outside dependency, which makes building faster, steadier and at home on a phone.
Why is the app this small?
There are hundreds of megabytes between this and the tools it stands beside. A compiler written for the job, and a package holding only what is needed, is the whole of the difference.
Which sites can Web To Apk wrap?
Any site that loads in a browser. The address is opened in a WebView inside your own package, so what the site can do there is what it can do in a browser.
Can a project be moved or deleted?
Yes. A project is a plain folder: move it, copy it, back it up or delete it with any file manager. Deleting one from here sends it to the trash, where it waits a day.
